user.title: Casambi gateway
user.description:
This integration talks to your Casambi luminaires through a Lithernet gateway over MQTT.

The MQTT broker Home Assistant uses is `{broker}` on port `{port}`.{broker_note} Note it down, you will enter it in the gateway in the next step.

The integration never connects to the gateway's web interface. You make the settings there yourself, and this wizard checks afterwards that everything arrives.

gateway.title: Connect the gateway to MQTT
gateway.description:
Open the gateway's web interface and go to Control System.

Enter the broker address `{broker}` and port `{port}` under **MQTT IP**, plus a user that exists on your broker.{broker_note}

**Careful, two similar fields:** `IP-Settings` is the gateway's own address. The broker belongs under `Control System`. Mixing them up creates an address conflict.

The bridge ID becomes part of every topic and is 0 in most installations.

data_description.gateway_host: Only used for the link to the web interface. The integration never connects there.
data_description.bridge_id: The number in topics such as casambi/0/set/target_level.

polling.title: Polling method
polling.description:
In the gateway under Casambi Settings you decide whether Home Assistant sees any state at all.

**inactive** sends nothing. Commands work, Home Assistant stays blind.
**active** polls all units in a cycle, roughly seven seconds delay.
**passive_37_80** reports changes immediately, about 0.16 seconds, and polls in quiet periods. This is the recommended setting.
**passive_37_90** and **passive_39_52** are faster still but need newer Casambi firmware on the luminaires themselves.

Also check the poll range: it has to cover every unit ID you want to use.

Select what you set in the gateway.

data.polling_method: Polling method set in the gateway

polling_inactive.title: Polling is inactive
polling_inactive.description:
You said the gateway is set to **inactive**. It then sends no state at all, so there is nothing to listen for and the state check is skipped.

Every luminaire will be operated blind: Home Assistant shows it as a device with separate on and off buttons and never learns whether it is on. If you would rather avoid that, go back and pick a passive polling method.

hints.title: Two more settings
hints.description:
**Use Broadcast** stays off. It controls Bluetooth broadcast and has nothing to do with MQTT.

Give the gateway a **fixed IP address** so its web interface stays reachable.

When both are done, continue to the check.

verify_command.title: Check: do commands arrive?
verify_command.description: Enter the Casambi unit ID of a luminaire you can see right now. It will switch to full brightness briefly and then off again.

verify_blink.title: Did the luminaire react?
verify_blink.description: Unit {unit_id} was told to go to full brightness and back off.

blink_no.title: Commands do not arrive
blink_no.description:
Check these three things in the gateway:

1. **MQTT IP** points at `{broker}`, not at the gateway itself.
2. The **user and password** exist on your broker.
3. The **bridge ID** matches the one you entered here ({bridge_id}).

Then try again.

verify_state.title: Check: does state come back?
verify_state.description: Now operate any luminaire in the Casambi app. The integration listens for {seconds} seconds and reports what arrives.

verify_state_result.title: Result of the state check

no_state.title: No state arrives
no_state.description:
In {seconds} seconds nothing came back. By far the most likely cause is the polling method being set to **inactive** in the gateway.

You can set it and listen again, or continue now. Without state every luminaire has to be operated blind, which Home Assistant shows as a device with separate on and off buttons.

multi_dali.title: Unit with several DALI drivers
multi_dali.description:
One Casambi unit drives several luminaires. Each driver becomes its own entity.

The gateway only reports a mixed value for the whole unit, so the individual entities are operated blind.

group.title: Casambi group
group.description:
Controls a group defined in the Casambi app with a single radio command.

For merely grouping entities in Home Assistant, a Home Assistant light group is the better tool.

switch.title: Switching output
switch.description:
A Casambi unit that only knows on and off, such as a fan.

Any run-on time belongs in a Home Assistant automation, not here.

mqtt_missing.title: MQTT is not available
mqtt_missing.description: The Casambi integration talks to the gateway through the MQTT integration, which is not set up. Add the MQTT integration, then reload Casambi.

no_state_received.title: No state from the Casambi gateway
no_state_received.description:
Nothing has arrived from the gateway for a day, although the polling method is not set to inactive here.

Check in the gateway under Casambi Settings that **Polling Method** is set to `passive_37_80` and that the poll range covers all your unit IDs.
